ch23.title: The Ordination on the Mount
ch23.b002: It was just before noon on Sunday, January 12, A.D. 27. The twelve had been expecting a summons almost any day, and so that morning they had not gone far from the shore to fish. Several of them lingered at the water’s edge, repairing their nets and tinkering with their fishing gear.
ch23.b003: Then Jesus came walking down the seashore. He first hailed Andrew and Peter, who were fishing near the shore; next he signaled to James and John, who sat in a boat near by with their father, Zebedee, mending their nets. Two by two he gathered up the others, and when all twelve had come, he led them up into the highlands north of Capernaum to instruct them in preparation for their formal ordination.
ch23.b004: On the way up no one spoke. For once all twelve were silent; even Peter was in a reflective mood. At last the long-awaited hour had come. They were going apart with the Master to take part in some solemn ceremony of personal consecration and collective dedication to the sacred work of representing him in the proclamation of the coming of his Father’s kingdom.
ch23.b006: When they had reached the place, the twelve sat down about him, and Jesus spoke: “⟦Q 140:1.1⟧My brethren, this hour of the kingdom has come. I have brought you apart here with me to present you to the Father as ambassadors of the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” They had heard him speak of the kingdom in the synagogue when first they were called, and they had learned more while working with him in the cities around the lake. But now, he said, he had something more to tell them.
ch23.b007: The new kingdom which his Father was about to set up in the hearts of his earth children was to be an everlasting dominion, with no end to the Father’s rule in those who desired to do his will. His Father was not the God of Jew or gentile; many would come from the east and the west to sit down in that kingdom, while many children of Abraham would refuse to enter. Its power would lie not in the strength of armies or the might of riches, but in the glory of the divine spirit that would come to teach the minds and rule the hearts of the reborn sons of God. “⟦Q 140:1.3⟧This is the brotherhood of love wherein righteousness reigns, and whose battle cry shall be: Peace on earth and good will to all men.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b008: Yet a severe test was set for them. Faith alone would pass them through its portals, but they must bring forth the fruits of the Father’s spirit if they would continue to ascend in the life of divine fellowship. “⟦Q 140:1.4⟧Verily, verily, I say to you, not every one who says, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven; but rather he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.⟦/Q⟧” Their message to the world was to be: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness. And this kingdom would not come with an outward show of power. “⟦Q 140:1.5⟧You are not to go hence in the proclamation of the kingdom, saying, ‘it is here’ or ‘it is there,’ for this kingdom of which you preach is God within you.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b009: Whoever would be first among them must become the server of his brethren; yet once they were truly received as citizens of the heavenly kingdom, they would no longer be servants but sons, sons of the living God. “⟦Q 140:1.7⟧And this which your eyes now behold, this small beginning of twelve commonplace men, shall multiply and grow until eventually the whole earth shall be filled with the praise of my Father. And it will not be so much by the words you speak as by the lives you live that men will know you have been with me.⟦/Q⟧” He would lay no grievous burdens on them, but he was about to put upon their souls the solemn responsibility of representing him in the world when he left them, as he now represented his Father in the flesh. And when he had finished speaking, he stood up.
ch23.b011: Jesus now told the twelve to kneel in a circle about him. Then he placed his hands upon the head of each apostle, beginning with Judas Iscariot and ending with Andrew. When he had blessed them all, he extended his hands and prayed:
ch23.b013: When the prayer was ended, the apostles remained each man bowed in his place. It was many minutes before even Peter dared lift his eyes to look upon the Master. Then one by one they rose and embraced him, but no man said anything. A great silence lay over the hillside, and unseen by any human eye a host of celestial beings looked down upon this solemn and sacred scene: the Creator of a universe placing the affairs of the divine brotherhood of man under the direction of human minds.
ch23.b015: Then Jesus spoke again. Now that they were ambassadors of his Father’s kingdom, they had become a class of men distinct from all others, like enlightened citizens of another and heavenly country living among the creatures of a dark world. “⟦Q 140:3.1⟧Of the teacher more is expected than of the pupil; of the master more is exacted than of the servant.⟦/Q⟧” Some of what he was about to say might seem hard, but they had chosen to represent him as he represented the Father. “I send you forth to proclaim liberty to the spiritual captives, joy to those in the bondage of fear, and to heal the sick in accordance with the will of my Father in heaven. When you find my children in distress, speak encouragingly to them, saying:
ch23.b025: The first four were attitudes of faith; the last four were the supreme reactions of fatherly love, a love that goes beyond the limits of mere brotherly love. Brotherly love would love one’s neighbor as oneself, but fatherly affection would love one’s fellow mortals as Jesus loves them. He did not ask the impossible of them, but he did expect them so to strive to be like God that they could begin to look upon men as God looks upon his creatures. The beatitudes were based on faith and love, not on law, ethics, and duty, and this momentous sermon began upon the note of happiness.
ch23.b026: “⟦Q 140:3.12⟧My brethren, as I send you forth, you are the salt of the earth, salt with a saving savor. But if this salt has lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted?⟦/Q⟧” In those days salt was precious, even used for money; it flavored food and preserved it, serving by being spent. “⟦Q 140:3.13⟧You are the light of the world. A city set upon a hill cannot be hid. … Let your light so shine before men that they may see your good works and be led to glorify your Father who is in heaven.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b027: He went on. They were not to resist injustice by force or put their trust in the arm of the flesh. If a neighbor struck them on the right cheek, they were to turn the other also. “⟦Q 140:3.15⟧I say to you: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who despitefully use you.⟦/Q⟧” The Father makes the sun to shine on the evil as well as the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust. “⟦Q 140:3.16⟧Be merciful, even as God is merciful.⟦/Q⟧” They were commissioned to save men, not to judge them; let each first cast the beam out of his own eye before plucking the mote from his brother’s. He warned them against false prophets who come in sheep’s clothing: “⟦Q 140:3.19⟧By their fruits you shall know them.⟦/Q⟧” In gaining entrance into the kingdom, it is the motive that counts, for the Father looks into the hearts of men and judges by their inner longings and sincere intentions.
ch23.b028: Never before had the apostles heard Jesus speak this way, for he talked to them as one having supreme authority. About sundown they came down from the mountain, but no man asked him a question. The so-called “Sermon on the Mount” is not the gospel of Jesus. It contains much helpful instruction, but it was his ordination charge to the twelve, his personal commission to those who were to represent him in the world of men as he so perfectly represented his Father.
ch23.b030: On reaching Zebedee’s home they shared a simple meal, and afterward Jesus went for a walk along the beach. The twelve talked among themselves, and while the twins built a small fire in the garden for warmth and light, Andrew went out to find the Master. “Master,” he said when he had overtaken him, “⟦Q 140:6.1⟧my brethren are unable to comprehend what you have said about the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” They did not feel able to begin the work without further instruction, and he asked Jesus to come and help them understand.
ch23.b031: So Jesus sat with them by the fire. They found his message hard, he said, because they would build the new teaching directly upon the old; they must be reborn and start afresh as little children. Yet they must not think he had come to set aside the law and the prophets: “⟦Q 140:6.2⟧I have not come to destroy but to fulfill, to enlarge and illuminate.⟦/Q⟧” When Peter asked to hear the new commandment, Jesus looked beyond the act to the motive. Whoever was angry with his brother, whoever looked upon a woman with intent to lust, already stood before judgment; men judge by deeds, but the Father judges by intent. James asked about divorce, and Jesus answered that he had come not to legislate but to enlighten, not to reform the kingdoms of this world but to establish the kingdom of heaven. Nathaniel asked about “an eye for an eye,” and Jesus said: “⟦Q 140:6.9⟧You shall return good for evil.⟦/Q⟧” Mercy must determine their judgments and love their conduct. “⟦Q 140:6.9⟧And if these are hard sayings, you can even now turn back. If you find the requirements of apostleship too hard, you may return to the less rigorous pathway of discipleship.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b032: The apostles drew apart for a while, but soon they returned, and Peter said: “⟦Q 140:6.10⟧Master, we would go on with you; not one of us would turn back. We are fully prepared to pay the extra price; we will drink the cup. We would be apostles, not merely disciples.⟦/Q⟧” Then Jesus told them to do their good deeds in secret, not to use vain repetitions in prayer, and to lay up treasures in heaven rather than on earth, “⟦Q 140:6.11⟧for where your treasures are, there will your hearts be also.⟦/Q⟧” When Thomas asked whether they should continue to have everything in common, he said that he wished them to live together as one understanding family. They were not to be anxious about what they would eat or wear. “⟦Q 140:6.13⟧Seek first the kingdom of God, and when you have found entrance thereto, all things needful shall be added to you.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b033: The night grew late, but no one wanted to sleep. “⟦Q 140:6.14⟧My brethren, you are earthen vessels,⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said; “⟦Q 140:6.14⟧it is best for you to go to your rest.⟦/Q⟧” But sleep had departed from their eyes. Peter asked for a little private talk: he had a troubled spirit, and if he deserved a rebuke, he could better bear it alone with his Master. Jesus said, “Come with me, Peter,” and led the way into the house. When Peter came out much cheered, James went in, and so on through the early hours of the morning each apostle sat alone with the Master. At last Andrew came in and asked whether he should wake the twins, who had fallen asleep by the fire in the garden. Jesus smiled. “They do well—trouble them not.” The night was passing, and the light of another day was dawning.
ch23.b035: After a few hours’ sleep, at a late breakfast, Jesus told them to make ready to go to Jerusalem. Thomas mustered his courage and said that, though they ought to be ready, he feared they were not yet able to accomplish so great an undertaking; would the Master consent to stay a few days more? Seeing that all of them shared this fear, Jesus said: “⟦Q 140:7.1⟧It shall be as you have requested; we will remain here over the Sabbath day.⟦/Q⟧” For weeks small groups of truth seekers and curious spectators had been coming to Bethsaida from as far away as Tyre, Sidon, Damascus, Caesarea, and Jerusalem. Now Jesus turned this work over to the twelve. For two days they taught by day and held private conferences late into the night; on the third they went fishing or visited their families; then came three more days of teaching. All that week Jesus repeated the two great motives of his mission: to reveal the Father to man, and to lead men to become son-conscious, to faith-realize that they are the children of the Most High. By the end some had grown over self-confident. At the last conference, the night after the Sabbath, Peter and James came to him saying, “⟦Q 140:7.7⟧We are ready—let us now go forth to take the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered, “⟦Q 140:7.7⟧May your wisdom equal your zeal and your courage atone for your ignorance.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b036: On the Thursday afternoon of that week Jesus had taken Peter, James, and John out on the lake in a boat for four hours of questions and answers. Trusting the Father, he told them, was not blind and passive fatalism; he quoted with approval the old saying, “⟦Q 140:8.2⟧He who will not work shall not eat.⟦/Q⟧” He taught them not to resist evil, yet he approved of the social punishment of criminals; he deplored revenge and the holding of grudges. He forbade them to become embroiled in the troubles between the Jews and Rome, ever answering, “⟦Q 140:8.9⟧Render to Caesar the things which are Caesar’s and to God the things which are God’s.⟦/Q⟧” He was not a political or economic reformer; he was concerned only with the principles of man’s inner and personal spiritual life. It was on this afternoon that he first told them “⟦Q 140:8.18⟧it is more blessed to give than to receive.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b037: He did not denounce wealth, but what wealth does to the majority of its devotees. The family stood at the very center of his philosophy of life, yet he did not hesitate to give up his family when it ran counter to the Father’s will. He was a positive teacher of true virtue who refused to advertise evil, and his few denunciations were directed against pride, cruelty, oppression, and hypocrisy. “Fear not” was his watchword, and courage the very heart of his teaching; that was why he chose rugged, manly fishermen as his representatives. From that afternoon John gained the understanding that the heart of Jesus’ religion was a compassionate character coupled with a personality motivated to do the Father’s will. Peter grasped that the gospel was a fresh beginning for the whole human race, and James the thrilling truth that Jesus wanted his children on earth to live as though they were already citizens of the completed heavenly kingdom. In answer to one of Peter’s many questions the Master said: “⟦Q 140:8.26⟧I want to set men free so that they can start out afresh as little children upon the new and better life.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b039: On the Sabbath Jesus took them back to the highland where he had ordained them. There was no new teaching that day, only visiting and communion. After a long and touching message of encouragement, he called them before him one by one and commissioned them: “⟦Q 140:9.2⟧Go into all the world and preach the glad tidings of the kingdom. Liberate spiritual captives, comfort the oppressed, and minister to the afflicted. Freely you have received, freely give.⟦/Q⟧” He told them to take neither money nor extra clothing, and finally he said: “⟦Q 140:9.3⟧Behold I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves; be you therefore as wise as serpents and as harmless as doves. … Some of you will be put to death, and before you establish the kingdom on earth, you will be hated by many peoples because of this gospel; but fear not; I will be with you, and my spirit shall go before you into all the world.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b040: That evening it began to rain, and in the house Jesus talked at great length, trying to show them what they must be rather than what they must do. “⟦Q 140:10.1⟧In the kingdom you must be righteous in order to do the work.⟦/Q⟧” What they could not gain from his words, they slowly acquired by living with him, for Jesus was all that he taught. When Simon Zelotes asked, “⟦Q 140:10.7⟧But, Master, are all men the sons of God?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 140:10.7⟧Yes, Simon, all men are the sons of God, and that is the good news you are going to proclaim.⟦/Q⟧” It was a new, strange, and startling announcement to them. Then John asked, “⟦Q 140:10.9⟧Master, what is the kingdom of heaven?⟦/Q⟧” And Jesus said: “⟦Q 140:10.9⟧The kingdom of heaven consists in these three essentials: first, recognition of the fact of the sovereignty of God; second, belief in the truth of sonship with God; and third, faith in the effectiveness of the supreme human desire to do the will of God—to be like God. And this is the good news of the gospel: that by faith every mortal may have all these essentials of salvation.⟦/Q⟧”
ch23.b041: The rain drummed on the roof of Zebedee’s house. The week of waiting was over, and on the morrow they would set out for Jerusalem.
part5: Part Five: The Gospel of the Kingdom
ch24.title: The Night Nicodemus Came
ch24.b002: On the first day of the week, January 19, A.D. 27, the yard before Zebedee’s house was crowded from early morning. The families of the apostles and many of the disciples had come to say good-bye and to wish them well in the new work. The twelve knew nothing of their Master’s plans except that they were going up to Jerusalem for the Passover in April, by way of the Jordan valley. The farewells went on so long that it was near noon before they were ready to leave.
ch24.b003: Just before setting out, the apostles missed the Master, and Andrew went to look for him. After a brief search he found Jesus sitting in a boat down the beach, and he was weeping. The twelve had often seen him grieve, and they had seen his brief seasons of serious preoccupation, but none of them had ever seen him weep. Somewhat startled, Andrew approached and asked: “⟦Q 141:0.2⟧On this great day, Master, when we are to depart for Jerusalem to proclaim the Father’s kingdom, why is it that you weep? Which of us has offended you?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus rose and went back with him to the others, answering: “⟦Q 141:0.2⟧No one of you has grieved me. I am saddened only because none of my father Joseph’s family have remembered to come over to bid us Godspeed.⟦/Q⟧” Ruth was at that time visiting her brother Joseph at Nazareth. The others had been kept away by pride, disappointment, misunderstanding, and petty resentment indulged as a result of hurt feelings.
ch24.b005: The fame of Jesus had begun to spread over all of Galilee and beyond, and Capernaum was not far from Tiberias, where Herod would soon take notice. So Jesus thought best to go south into Judea. More than a hundred believers wanted to go with them, and he besought them to stay behind; they consented, though many followed within a few days. The first night they rested at Tarichea, and the next day they came to a point on the Jordan near Pella, where John had preached about a year before and where Jesus had been baptized. They stayed more than two weeks, and by the end of the first week several hundred people had gathered in a camp near by, from Galilee, Phoenicia, Syria, the Decapolis, Perea, and Judea.
ch24.b006: Jesus did no public preaching. Andrew divided the multitude and assigned the apostles to preach in the forenoon and afternoon, and after the evening meal Jesus talked with the twelve, reviewing his teaching and answering their questions. One evening he told them something of the forty days he had spent in the hills near that very place. Many in the camp had been baptized by John, and one thing always troubled them: if Jesus were all that John had announced, why did he do nothing to get him out of prison? During this first year more than three fourths of Jesus’ followers had once followed John, and night after night Andrew instructed his fellows in the delicate task of getting along smoothly with them.
ch24.b007: The night before they left Pella, Jesus spoke to them of God’s law and the Father’s will. They had pictured the kingdom as a glorified rule of the Jewish people, with Messiah on David’s throne. But the kingdom of heaven is the realization and acknowledgment of God’s rule within the hearts of men, and its King is “my Father and your Father.” We are his loyal subjects, he said, but far beyond that is the transforming truth that we are his sons. “⟦Q 141:2.2⟧Verily, verily, I say to you, when the Father’s will is your law, you are hardly in the kingdom. But when the Father’s will becomes truly your will, then are you in very truth in the kingdom because the kingdom has thereby become an established experience in you.⟦/Q⟧” Some grasped something of this, but none comprehended its full significance, unless it was James Zebedee.
ch24.b008: They moved on to the neighborhood of Amathus and stayed almost three weeks. The apostles preached twice daily, and Jesus preached each Sabbath afternoon. There were constant misunderstandings between the disciples of John and the newer disciples of Jesus, and Andrew was kept busy settling them. Jesus refused to take part in any of these conferences or even to give advice. When Andrew brought him such problems, he would always say: “⟦Q 141:3.3⟧It is not wise for the host to participate in the family troubles of his guests; a wise parent never takes sides in the petty quarrels of his own children.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b009: At Amathus he impressed upon them again and again that God is a Father, not a great and supreme bookkeeper making damaging entries against his erring children. When Thomas asked, “⟦Q 141:4.2⟧Who is this God of the kingdom?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 141:4.2⟧God is your Father, and religion—my gospel—is nothing more nor less than the believing recognition of the truth that you are his son.⟦/Q⟧” He also began to teach them more fully about their mission “⟦Q 141:4.4⟧to comfort the afflicted and minister to the sick,⟦/Q⟧” showing them how to recognize diseases of the flesh, troubled minds, and the possession of evil spirits. One evening James Zebedee asked how they might learn to see alike and so enjoy more harmony among themselves. Jesus was stirred within his spirit. “⟦Q 141:5.1⟧James, James, when did I teach you that you should all see alike? I have come into the world to proclaim spiritual liberty to the end that mortals may be empowered to live individual lives of originality and freedom before God.⟦/Q⟧” What he required of them was spirit unity, born of the consciousness that each was indwelt by the same spirit gift of the Father, with a common motive, to do the Father’s will, and a common goal, to find the Father. “⟦Q 141:5.1⟧You do not have to see alike or feel alike or even think alike in order spiritually to be alike.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b010: Near the end of the last week Simon Zelotes brought to Jesus a Persian named Teherma, who did business at Damascus. Simon regarded him as a “fire worshiper” and had tried hard to persuade him, without success; yet Teherma listened readily to Jesus. When Simon asked why, Jesus answered: “⟦Q 141:6.2⟧Simon, Simon, how many times have I instructed you to refrain from all efforts to take something out of the hearts of those who seek salvation? How often have I told you to labor only to put something into these hungry souls? Lead men into the kingdom, and the great and living truths of the kingdom will presently drive out all serious error.⟦/Q⟧” Simon was astonished, but he did as he was told, and Teherma was numbered among those who entered the kingdom.
ch24.b012: On February 26 the company went down the Jordan to the ford near Bethany in Perea, the place where John had first proclaimed the coming kingdom, and they remained there four weeks. During the second week Jesus took Peter, James, and John into the hills across the river south of Jericho for three days’ rest. He told them that he had come not to set an example for a few earth creatures but to establish a standard of human life for all peoples on all worlds throughout his universe. They could not grasp it. Yet James was astonished at how Jesus seemed to see the end from the beginning; he was never excited or vexed, at times saddened but never discouraged. And John saw more clearly that, notwithstanding all his divine endowments, he was human, so human and yet so faultless.
ch24.b013: Several times a week Andrew sent pairs of apostles up to Jericho, where John had many believers. They went from house to house seeking to comfort every afflicted person, and they discovered that the good news of the kingdom was very comforting to the sick. It was in Jericho that the commission to preach the glad tidings and minister to the afflicted was first fully carried into effect. When they stopped there on the way to Jerusalem, a delegation from Mesopotamia overtook them, and Jesus spent three days with these truth seekers from the East, who went home along the Euphrates happy in the new truths of the kingdom.
ch24.b014: On Monday, the last day of March, they began the climb toward Jerusalem. Lazarus of Bethany had twice come down to the Jordan to see Jesus, and everything had been arranged for them to make his home their headquarters. For five days the Master and the twelve rested there, and it was a great event in the lives of Martha and Mary to have them in their brother’s house and to minister to their needs. Then, on Sunday morning, April 6, Jesus and the apostles went down to Jerusalem; it was the first time the Master and all twelve had been there together.
ch24.b016: On the first day Jesus called upon his friend of former years, Annas, the onetime high priest and a relative of Salome. Annas received him with much reserve. Perceiving his coldness, Jesus took immediate leave, saying as he went: “⟦Q 142:0.2⟧Fear is man’s chief enslaver and pride his great weakness; will you betray yourself into bondage to both of these destroyers of joy and liberty?⟦/Q⟧” Annas made no reply. The Master did not see him again until the day Annas sat with his son-in-law in judgment on the Son of Man.
ch24.b017: Throughout April, Jesus or one of the apostles taught daily in the temple, and when the Passover crowds were too great, the apostles gathered teaching groups outside the sacred precincts. Each evening they went out of the city to sleep at Bethany. The burden of their message was simple: the kingdom of heaven is at hand; by faith in the fatherhood of God men may enter it and become sons of God; love is the rule of living within the kingdom; and obedience to the Father’s will, yielding the fruits of the spirit, is its law. Hundreds rejoiced in the good news and carried it to the uttermost parts of the Roman Empire and to the East. The chief priests and rulers began to debate among themselves what should be done with Jesus and his apostles.
ch24.b018: One or two nights each week Jesus stayed in the city at the home of Flavius, a Greek Jew, where many prominent Jews came secretly to see him. There a wealthy trader from Crete named Jacob asked him how this kind and compassionate Father could be the jealous God of wrath of whom Moses and the prophets spoke. Jesus answered that the Father in Paradise is changeless, but man’s concept of his nature has enlarged and grown. “⟦Q 142:2.3⟧You, Jacob, being a father of many, know well the truth of my words.⟦/Q⟧” Jacob asked how he knew that he was the father of six children. “⟦Q 142:2.3⟧Suffice it to say that the Father and the Son know all things, for indeed they see all.⟦/Q⟧” Young children who are chastised may think their father angry, Jesus went on, but grown men and women should discern their father’s love in all those early disciplines; should not mankind, as the centuries pass, come to understand the Father in heaven better? And Jacob answered: “⟦Q 142:2.5⟧Rabbi, I believe; I desire that you lead me into the Father’s kingdom.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b019: Flavius’s house was a beautiful edifice, adorned with statues and treasures gathered on his travels, and he had feared that the Master might take offense at these so-called images. Instead Jesus showed great interest in the whole collection and asked many appreciative questions as they went from room to room. Seeing his host bewildered, he said: “⟦Q 142:4.2⟧Because you appreciate the beauty of things created by my Father and fashioned by the artistic hands of man, why should you expect to be rebuked?⟦/Q⟧” In the coming kingdom, he said, men would be concerned with one supreme duty, expressed in two great privileges: sincere worship of the Paradise Father and loving service to one’s fellow men. Flavius believed all that Jesus taught him, and the next day he went to Bethany beyond the Jordan and was baptized by the disciples of John.
ch24.b021: One evening there came to the house of Flavius a man named Nicodemus, a wealthy and elderly member of the Sanhedrin. He had gone one afternoon to hear Jesus in the temple courts and would have gone often, but he feared to be seen, for the rulers of the Jews were already so at variance with Jesus that no member of the Sanhedrin wished to be openly identified with him. So he had arranged with Andrew to see the Master privately after nightfall. He did not come as a delegate of the Sanhedrin; he came wholly out of his own sincere interest.
ch24.b022: Peter, James, and John were in the garden when the interview began, and later they all went into the house as the talk went on. Jesus showed his distinguished visitor no particular deference; there was no compromise, no undue persuasion, no attempt to repulse him, no sarcasm. He was calm, earnest, and dignified. When Flavius had presented him, Nicodemus said: “⟦Q 142:6.3⟧Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent by God, for no mere man could so teach unless God were with him. And I am desirous of knowing more about your teachings regarding the coming kingdom.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b023: Jesus answered: “⟦Q 142:6.4⟧Verily, verily, I say to you, Nicodemus, except a man be born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God.⟦/Q⟧” Nicodemus replied: “⟦Q 142:6.4⟧But how can a man be born again when he is old? He cannot enter a second time into his mother’s womb to be born.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b024: Jesus said: “⟦Q 142:6.5⟧Nevertheless, I declare to you, except a man be born of the spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the spirit is spirit. But you should not marvel that I said you must be born from above. When the wind blows, you hear the rustle of the leaves, but you do not see the wind—whence it comes or whither it goes—and so it is with everyone born of the spirit.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b025: “⟦Q 142:6.6⟧But I do not understand—how can that be?⟦/Q⟧” said Nicodemus. Jesus asked whether a teacher in Israel could be ignorant of all this, and then: “⟦Q 142:6.6⟧Do you have the courage, Nicodemus, to believe in one who has descended from heaven, even the Son of Man?⟦/Q⟧” Nicodemus asked how he could begin to lay hold upon this spirit which was to remake him. Jesus answered: “⟦Q 142:6.7⟧Already does the spirit of the Father in heaven indwell you. If you would be led by this spirit from above, very soon would you begin to see with the eyes of the spirit, and then by the wholehearted choice of spirit guidance would you be born of the spirit since your only purpose in living would be to do the will of your Father who is in heaven.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b026: Nicodemus was thoroughly sincere. He went away deeply impressed but bewildered. He was accomplished in self-development and self-restraint, a man of high moral qualities, refined and altruistic; but he did not know how to submit his will to the will of the divine Father as a little child submits to the guidance of a wise and loving earthly father. Yet he did summon faith enough to lay hold of the kingdom. He would faintly protest when his colleagues of the Sanhedrin sought to condemn Jesus without a hearing, and with Joseph of Arimathea he would later boldly claim the body of Jesus, when most of the disciples had fled in fear.
ch24.b028: On the Wednesday after Passover week, resting at Bethany, Thomas asked what they should teach the multitude about how to live once the kingdom more fully came. Should believers own slaves, court poverty, abandon law and justice? Jesus spent the afternoon and evening speaking of the earthly family as an illustration of the heavenly family. When Thomas was still not satisfied, the Master implored them to stop applying the teaching of the spirit kingdom to the affairs of slavery, poverty, houses, and lands. “⟦Q 142:7.17⟧Nevertheless, I love you and will bear with you, even to the very end of our association in the flesh. And even then shall my spirit go before you into all the world.⟦/Q⟧”
ch24.b029: By the end of April the opposition of the Pharisees and Sadducees had grown so pronounced that the company left Jerusalem and spent the whole of May in Bethlehem and Hebron, doing no public preaching, only house-to-house visitation. For part of that time Jesus and Abner went to Engedi to visit the Nazarite colony from which John the Baptist had gone forth. Many of the brotherhood believed in Jesus, but most refused him because he did not teach fasting and self-denial. The people of that region did not know that Jesus had been born in Bethlehem; they supposed, as most of his disciples did, that he was born at Nazareth.
ch24.b030: In June they returned and lived mostly in tents pitched in a shaded garden on the western slope of the Mount of Olives, not far from the brook Kidron, a place then known as Gethsemane. Jesus seldom entered the city, but many inquirers came out to him. One Friday evening Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea ventured out to see him, but even after they stood before the entrance of his tent, they turned back through fear. They did not perceive that Jesus knew all about their doings. Things went on quietly until the last days of June, when Simon, a member of the Sanhedrin, publicly espoused Jesus’ teachings. At once a new agitation for his arrest sprang up, and the Master decided to retire into the cities of Samaria and the Decapolis.
ch25.title: At Jacob's Well
ch25.b002: At the end of June, A.D. 27, Jesus and the twelve sent their tents and meager belongings to be stored at the home of Lazarus in Bethany and set out northward into Samaria. They tarried over the Sabbath at Bethel and preached for several days to people from Gophna and Ephraim. Citizens of Arimathea and Thamna came to invite them to their villages, and others came from as far as Antipatris to hear the good news. The people of southern Samaria heard Jesus gladly, and the apostles overcame much of their old prejudice against the Samaritans, all except Judas Iscariot, who found it very difficult to love them.
ch25.b003: The first half of August they spent in the new Greek cities of Archelais and Phasaelis near the Jordan, where few Jews lived. For the first time the apostles preached to gatherings almost wholly gentile, Greeks, Romans, and Syrians, and they met new objections. At an evening conference Philip put their difficulty: “⟦Q 143:1.2⟧Master, these Greeks and Romans make light of our message, saying that such teachings are fit for only weaklings and slaves.⟦/Q⟧” They claimed their own religion built strong, robust, aggressive character. “⟦Q 143:1.2⟧They like you, Master, and freely admit that your teaching is heavenly and ideal, but they will not take us seriously. … And now, Master, what shall we say to these gentiles?⟦/Q⟧”
ch25.b004: Jesus listened while Thomas, Nathaniel, Simon Zelotes, and Matthew told of similar objections, and then he answered with a strong feeling he seldom showed. “⟦Q 143:1.5⟧But who told you that my gospel was intended only for slaves and weaklings? Do you, my chosen apostles, resemble weaklings? Did John look like a weakling? Do you observe that I am enslaved by fear?⟦/Q⟧” The Paradise ascent, he said, is the supreme adventure of all time, and the service of the kingdom would call for all the courageous manhood they could muster. It is easy to die in battle beside one’s comrades, but it requires a more profound courage calmly and all alone to lay down one’s life for the love of a truth enshrined in the heart. “⟦Q 143:1.7⟧The courage of the flesh is the lowest form of bravery. Mind bravery is a higher type of human courage, but the highest and supreme is uncompromising loyalty to the enlightened convictions of profound spiritual realities.⟦/Q⟧” From that very day their preaching took on a new note of courageous dominance.
ch25.b006: About this time a great nervous and emotional tension developed among the apostles. They had hardly become used to living and working together; they had increasing trouble keeping peace with John’s disciples; contact with gentiles and Samaritans was a great trial to them; and the Master’s recent words had stirred them further. Andrew was almost beside himself. When he brought his perplexities to Jesus, the Master said: “⟦Q 143:3.1⟧Andrew, you cannot talk men out of their perplexities when they reach such a stage of involvement.⟦/Q⟧” He would not take part in these personal difficulties, but he would join them in three days of rest. Andrew was to go to each of his eleven brethren privately and ask him to make no mention of their trials and troubles while they were on holiday. And Andrew did so.
ch25.b007: They never forgot the day they went up the mountain. On the summit Jesus seated them about him and said: “⟦Q 143:3.3⟧My brethren, you must all learn the value of rest and the efficacy of relaxation. You must realize that the best method of solving some entangled problems is to forsake them for a time.⟦/Q⟧” The next day he gave each a topic to discuss, and the whole day went to reminiscences and to matters unrelated to their religious work. They were momentarily shocked when, breaking bread at noon, he did not even give thanks aloud; it was the first time they had seen him neglect such a formality. They had gone up full of troubles: Andrew’s head crowded with problems, Matthew short of funds, Peter overwrought, Thomas deep in depression; only the twins were normal and unperturbed. But on the third day, when they started down, a great change had come over them. They had discovered that many human perplexities are in reality nonexistent, the creations of exaggerated fear, and that by going off they had left such problems to solve themselves. Many of them gave way to mirth when they saw the changed state of everybody’s mind, and from that time relations with John’s followers greatly improved.
ch25.b008: On a Monday morning about the middle of the month, Jesus said to Andrew: “We go into Samaria.”
ch25.b010: For more than six hundred years the Jews had been at enmity with the Samaritans. About seven hundred years B.C., Sargon, king of Assyria, had carried away more than twenty-five thousand Jews of the northern kingdom and installed in their place almost as many foreign colonists. When the Jews returned from the Babylonian captivity, the Samaritans worked to prevent the rebuilding of Jerusalem; later they gave friendly help to the armies of Alexander, who in return allowed them to build a temple on Mount Gerizim. John Hyrcanus destroyed that temple in the time of the Maccabees, and increasingly since the days of Alexander the two peoples had had no dealings with each other.
ch25.b011: The apostles were not averse to preaching in Greek cities, but it was a severe test of their loyalty when the Master said, “Let us go into Samaria.” Yet in the year and more they had been with him, they had developed a personal loyalty that transcended even their prejudices against the Samaritans. They set out at once for the city of Sychar, near Jacob’s well.
ch25.b013: When they arrived at the well, Jesus was weary from the journey and stayed there while Philip took the others into Sychar to bring food and tents. Peter and the sons of Zebedee would have remained, but he sent them with their brethren, saying: “⟦Q 143:5.1⟧Have no fear for me; these Samaritans will be friendly; only our brethren, the Jews, seek to harm us.⟦/Q⟧” It was almost six o’clock on that summer evening when he sat down by the well to wait.
ch25.b014: The water of Jacob’s well was less mineral than that of the wells of Sychar and was much valued for drinking. Jesus was thirsty, but he had nothing to draw with. When a woman of Sychar came with her water pitcher, he said to her, “Give me a drink.” Her name was Nalda, and she was a comely woman. She knew him for a Jew by his dress and a Galilean by his accent, and she was much surprised, for it was not thought proper for a self-respecting man to speak to a woman in public, still less for a Jew to speak to a Samaritan. “⟦Q 143:5.2⟧How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink of me, a Samaritan woman?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 143:5.2⟧I have indeed asked you for a drink, but if you could only understand, you would ask me for a draught of the living water.⟦/Q⟧”
ch25.b015: Nalda asked how, with nothing to draw with and the well so deep, he could have living water, and whether he was greater than their father Jacob, who had given them this well. Jesus replied: “⟦Q 143:5.3⟧Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, but whosoever drinks of the water of the living spirit shall never thirst. And this living water shall become in him a well of refreshment springing up even to eternal life.⟦/Q⟧” Then give me this water, she said, so that I need not come all the way here to draw.
ch25.b016: Nalda did not know how to take his willingness to talk with her. She saw in his face the countenance of an upright and holy man, but she mistook his friendliness for commonplace familiarity, and being a woman of lax morals, she was minded openly to become flirtatious. Then Jesus, looking straight into her eyes, said with a commanding voice, “⟦Q 143:5.4⟧Woman, go get your husband and bring him hither.⟦/Q⟧” The command brought her to her senses. She saw that she had misjudged him and grew frightened, realizing she stood before an unusual person. In confusion she said she had no husband. Jesus said: “⟦Q 143:5.4⟧You have spoken the truth, for, while you may have once had a husband, he with whom you are now living is not your husband. Better it would be if you would cease to trifle with my words and seek for the living water which I have this day offered you.⟦/Q⟧”
ch25.b017: Now Nalda was sobered, and her better self was awakened. She was not an immoral woman wholly by choice. Her husband had ruthlessly and unjustly cast her aside, and in dire straits she had consented to live with a certain Greek without marriage. Ashamed, she told Jesus that she repented of her manner of speaking, for she perceived he was a holy man or perhaps a prophet. But just as she was about to ask for help, she did what so many have done before and since: she dodged the issue of personal salvation by turning to theology. Pointing to Mount Gerizim, she asked whether the right place to worship God was this mountain, where her fathers had worshiped, or Jerusalem.
ch25.b018: Jesus perceived the attempt of her soul to avoid direct contact with its Maker, but he saw too that there was in her heart a true thirst for the living water, and he dealt patiently with her: “⟦Q 143:5.6⟧But you should believe me when I say that the hour will soon come—even now is—when all sincere worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for it is just such worshipers the Father seeks. God is spirit, and they who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. Your salvation comes not from knowing how others should worship or where but by receiving into your own heart this living water which I am offering you even now.⟦/Q⟧”
ch25.b019: Once more Nalda tried to turn aside. She knew, she said, that John had preached about the coming of the Converter, the Deliverer, who would declare all things. Jesus interrupted her and said with startling assurance, “⟦Q 143:5.7⟧I who speak to you am he.⟦/Q⟧”
ch25.b020: This was the first direct, positive, and undisguised pronouncement of his divine nature and sonship that Jesus had made on earth. It was made to a woman, a Samaritan woman, a woman of questionable character in the eyes of men; but the divine eye beheld her as one who had been sinned against more than sinning of her own desire, a human soul who now sincerely and wholeheartedly desired salvation. And that was enough.
ch25.b021: Just as she was ready to speak the real desire of her heart, the twelve came back from Sychar. Finding the Master talking so intimately, and alone, with a Samaritan woman, they were more than astonished. They set down their supplies and drew aside, no man daring to reprove him, while Jesus said to Nalda: “⟦Q 143:5.9⟧Woman, go your way; God has forgiven you. Henceforth you will live a new life. You have received the living water, and a new joy will spring up within your soul, and you shall become a daughter of the Most High.⟦/Q⟧” Feeling the disapproval of the apostles, she left her waterpot and fled to the city.
ch25.b023: To everyone she met in Sychar, Nalda cried: “⟦Q 143:5.10⟧Go out to Jacob’s well and go quickly, for there you will see a man who told me all I ever did. Can this be the Converter?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus had told her only one thing about herself. But his look into her eyes and his manner with her had brought her whole checkered life before her mind in a moment, and she associated all of it with his word. Before the sun went down, a great crowd had gathered at the well.
ch25.b024: The twelve, who had eaten nothing all day, begged him to eat before he spoke to the people. “⟦Q 143:6.1⟧I have meat to eat that you do not know about,⟦/Q⟧” he said. They asked one another whether the woman had given him food as well as drink. Then he turned to them: “⟦Q 143:6.1⟧My meat is to do the will of Him who sent me and to accomplish His work. … Behold these people coming out from a Samaritan city to hear us; I tell you the fields are already white for the harvest.⟦/Q⟧” Others had labored, he said, and they were about to enter into their labor; he was speaking of the preaching of John the Baptist. Then, as darkness came on, he talked to the crowd about the water of life, the gift of the indwelling spirit.
ch25.b025: They preached two days in Sychar and then made camp on Mount Gerizim. The first night the apostles expected a rebuke for their attitude toward the woman at the well, but Jesus made no reference to it. Instead he spoke of the realities central in the kingdom: that he wanted all men to see God as a Father-friend, just as he was a brother-friend, and that love is the greatest relationship in the universe. He declared himself so fully to the Samaritans because he could safely do so, and because he knew he would not again visit the heart of Samaria to preach.
ch25.b026: Until the end of August they camped on Mount Gerizim, preaching the fatherhood of God in the Samaritan cities by day and returning to camp at night. In the evenings Jesus taught them about prayer and worship. Prayer, he taught, is designed to make man less thinking but more realizing; it is not designed to increase knowledge but rather to expand insight. Worship, he said, is the act of a part identifying itself with the Whole, the son with the Father, time in the act of striking step with eternity. The apostles grasped only a few of these teachings. But the work they did in those cities yielded many souls for the kingdom and prepared the way for the marvelous harvest Philip would gather there after the persecutions had scattered the believers.
